title: Impact of a patient advisory board on the development of smart implants for musculoskeletal care: a longitudinal mixed-methods evaluation study
summary:
Conditions affecting bones, joints and muscles are common. They can cause chronic pain, limit mobility and reduce quality of life. As the proportion of older people in the population increases, these conditions and the associated need for care are expected to increase. New health technologies may help adapt care more closely to individual needs.

The EU-funded SmILE research project is therefore developing smart implants. Using built-in sensors and a digital health platform, these implants are intended to monitor healing, detect possible complications early and enable individual treatment recommendations. Patient advisory boards in Germany, Portugal and Luxembourg contribute to the development process to ensure that the needs and experiences of potential future users are considered.

This study examines the involvement of the German SmILE patient advisory board and its impact on the project. We want to find out how advisory board members assess their involvement and to what extent their contributions are considered during development. We also examine how researchers experience working with the advisory board and what makes meaningful involvement easier or more difficult.

Advisory board members will be asked to complete a questionnaire once a year for three years about their experiences during the preceding year. Researchers who have worked with the advisory board will also be invited to interviews. In addition, we will keep a record of the advisory board’s contributions, the decisions taken about them and any resulting changes. Members’ questionnaire responses will be compared with these records. The interviews will add the researchers’ perspectives. The findings are intended to improve patient involvement within SmILE and in future research projects.
conditions: Disorders of bone density and structure
Injury of muscle and tendon at shoulder and upper arm level
Injuries to the hip and thigh
Injuries to the knee and lower leg
Fracture of lower limb, level unspecified

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Quantitative survey: Membership of the German SmILE patient advisory board during the respective reference period and informed consent to study participation and data processing.

Qualitative interviews: Researchers in the SmILE consortium who have interacted with the German patient advisory board at least once during the respective reference period and provide written informed consent to study participation and data processing.
Exclusion criteria:
No additional exclusion criteria.
